entries.def: [formal/written style]
entries.example: I had written to her prior to meeting the committee.

entries.def: [fairly formal, more informal would be Before that, I ...]
entries.example: It was nice to be in Venice. Previously I'd only been to Rome.

entries.def: [before then, fairly informal]
entries.example: I was in the office from 2.30. I was out earlier on.

entries.def: [fairly formal, typically written; used when something has changed its name, state, etc.]
entries.example: The city is now called Thatcherville. Formerly it was Grabtown.

entries.def: [or, more formal: While waiting, I read ...; the waiting and reading happen together.]
entries.example: While I waited, I read the newspaper.
entries.group: Things happening at the same time

entries.def: [As describes the background when something happens in the foreground. As cannot be immediately followed by -ing.]
entries.example: As I was driving to work, I saw an accident.
entries.group: Things happening at the same time

entries.def: [precise moment]
entries.example: I saw her just as she was turning the corner.
entries.group: Things happening at the same time

entries.word: at the very time / the very moment
entries.def: [these two are stronger and more precise than as or just as]
entries.example: She was entering at the very time / the very moment I was leaving.
entries.group: Things happening at the same time

entries.def: [every time]
entries.example: Whenever I watch a sad film, I cry.
entries.group: Things happening at the same time

entries.def: During does not specify how long within a period of time.
entries.example: During the war, I lived in Dublin.
entries.group: Things happening at the same time

entries.def: Throughout means from the beginning to the end of a period of time.
entries.example: Throughout the war, food was rationed.
entries.group: Things happening at the same time

entries.def: [or, more formal: After locking up; we do not usually say 'After having locked up ...', which is very formal style.]
entries.example: After I'd locked up, I went to bed.
First we went to theatre. Then / After that, we had a meal.

entries.def: [In these two examples, after that and afterwards are interchangeable.]
entries.example: He fell ill and was admitted to hospital. He died soon afterwards.

entries.def: [fairly formal]
entries.example: Following my visit to Beijing, I bought several books about China.

entries.def: [Don't say: 'When I will be rich ...']
entries.example: When I'm rich and famous, I'll buy a yacht.

entries.def: [immediately after]
entries.example: As soon as we've packed we can leave.

entries.def: [less specific]
entries.example: Once we've finished we can go and have a coffee.
The moment/the minute I saw his face I knew I'd met him before.
I stayed in that hospital the time (that) I broke my leg.

entries.def: [more formal]
entries.example: I met Polly at Ken's wedding. On that occasion she was with a different man.

entries.def: [between now and the meal]
entries.example: Dinner will be ready in about an hour. In the meantime, relax and have a drink.
The new computers are arriving soon. Till then, we'll have to use the old ones.
I last met him in 1985. Since then I haven't seen him.

entries.def: [Don't say: 'By the time I will retire ...']
entries.example: By the time I retire, I will have worked here 26 years.

note: Presentation is a connector list in sections A–E; bold headwords embedded in example sentences with square-bracket printed glosses. Bracket glosses copied into 'def' as printed (no '(=)' style glosses on this page). Exercise page 45 excluded.
